title: product-prd-overview-roadmap-pricing-and-release-2026-11-20
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Product overview

Summary
This document consolidates the product overview, high-level PRD requirements, design considerations, roadmap and themes, pricing and packaging guidance, and the release notes for the Unified Inference effort and associated Optimize features. It is intended for PMs, Eng leads, Sales enablement, and GTM partners preparing for customer conversations and launch activities.

1) Product overview
- Product name: Unified Inference + Redwood Optimize (bundle capabilities)
- Goal: Provide a single API and operational model for high-performance LLM inference across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments while offering cost and quality controls for production workloads.
- Primary users: software engineers, ML engineers, platform teams.
- Key differentiators:
  - Unified runtime and API across deployment modes (hosted, dedicated, private)
  - Cost-aware controls: batching, caching, quantization recommendations
  - Production-first observability and rollout tools (per-route dashboards, canary/A-B)

2) PRD and high-level requirements (MUST / SHOULD / NICE-TO-HAVE)
- Context: This PRD covers the Unified Inference v7 milestone (QA and GA of routing, model variants, and cost controls) and Redwood Optimize v6 integrations.

MUST:
- API: stable HTTP/SDK surfaces for text generation, chat, embeddings, and reranking with backward-compatible schema.
- SLOs: 99.9% uptime for hosted endpoints; p50/p95/p99 latency targets published per-model.
- Fallback routing: automated policy-based fallback to compatible model variants on capacity or error thresholds.
- Cost controls: per-route batching and prefix caching settings surfaced in Console and configurable via API.
- Security: customer data isolation for Dedicated plans and private control plane for Private deployments; support for KMS integrations.
- Rollouts: support canary and A/B deploys with automatic rollback on quality regressions or increased error rate.

SHOULD:
- Quantization recommendations: automated suggestion engine that recommends INT8/4 quantization profiles per model by workload.
- Recommendations: suggestion UI in Console showing expected cost delta and latency change.
- Eval integration: tie eval sets to rollout gating (promote/rollback based on eval thresholds).

NICE-TO-HAVE:
- Auto-tier routing: dynamic routing that balances cost vs latency in real-time based on load.

Requirements table (condensed)
| Requirement ID | Title | Priority | Owner | Verification Criteria | Notes |
| RQ-API-01 | Stable API surface | MUST | API Platform | Backward compatibility tests pass; SDKs updated | Registry of breaking changes |
| RQ-SLO-01 | Published SLOs | MUST | SRE/Product | Dashboards created; alerting configured | p99 latency SLA depends on model family |
| RQ-ROUTE-01 | Policy-based routing & fallback | MUST | Serving Runtime | Chaos tests simulate node loss; fallback engaged | Support region-aware policies |
| RQ-COST-01 | Per-route cost controls | MUST | Product/Optimize | Console shows suggestions; API accepts overrides | Expose estimated cost impact |

3) Design specs and architecture notes
- Runtime architecture summary:
  - Request flow: Router -> Model Selection -> Serving Runtime -> KV/Prefix Cache -> Response Stream
  - Kernel selection: compilation service selects kernel profiles based on model architecture and sequence length distribution.
  - Caching: prefix/KV cache is sharded by customer and route; cache hit metrics recorded for cost analytics.

- Components and owners:
  - Router & Policies (eng-serving-runtime): owner: Priya Narang
  - Model Catalog & Variants (applied-ml-and-evals): owner: Diego Ramirez
  - Console & Recommendations (eng-developer-experience + product): owner: Aisha Patel
  - Billing & Cost Estimator (finance-and-legal + eng-platform): owner: Marco Li

- Compatibility matrix (example):
  - Model A (LLAMA-4-30B): recommended quantization: q4_0; expected p95 latency (A100): 120ms; compatible fallback: Model A-quantized, Model B-small
  - Model B (Redwood-1-7B): recommended: q8_0; expected p95 latency (A10G): 80ms; fallback: Model B-quantized

Design constraints and tradeoffs:
- Batching vs latency: default adaptive batching aims to maximize throughput without violating per-request latency SLOs.
- Cache memory vs hit rate: shard-level cache sizes are tunable per-customer to avoid noisy neighbor eviction.

4) Roadmap and themes (next 9 months)
- Themes by quarter:
  - Q4 2026: GA of Unified Inference v7 (routing + fallback), Redwood Optimize v6 rollout, Console cost-suggestion MVP, Pricing pilot for Reserved Dedicated bundles.
  - Q1 2027: Private control plane GA for select customers, improved quantization recommendations & one-click apply, per-route eval gating.
  - Q2 2027: Auto-tier routing beta, longer retention for observability (paid add-on), marketplace packaging for cloud partners.

Roadmap milestones (high-level):
1. Feature complete: policy-based routing and fallback (2026-11-30) - owner: Priya Narang
2. Console cost-suggestion MVP (2026-12-15) - owner: Aisha Patel
3. Optimize integration (2027-01-31) - owner: Marco Li
4. Dedicated pricing pilot (2027-02-15) - owner: Sales Ops
5. Private control plane GA (2027-03-31) - owner: Eng Private Deployments

5) Pricing and packaging notes
- Pricing principles:
  - Transparent, usage-based for Hosted (per-token & per-embedding) with recommended default conservative throttles.
  - Committed Reserved pricing for Dedicated capacity (monthly/annual) with tiered discounts based on GPU class and commit size.
  - Private deployment: platform fee + optional support/operational add-ons.

- Suggested packaging for launch:
  - Hosted: Pay-as-you-go (standard rate) + Optimize add-on (flat monthly + % savings guarantee pilot).
  - Dedicated: Bronze/Silver/Gold reserved capacity tiers (commit ranges + SLA levels).
  - Private: Base license + integration fee + optional SOC2/PCI compliance package.

- Example pricing matrix (illustrative numbers)
| Plan | Billing model | Key features | Target customer |
| Hosted Standard | Per-token | Model catalog, Console, Basic SLO | Early-stage startups |
| Dedicated Bronze | Monthly commit | Reserved GPU pool, 99.95% uptime | Mid-market teams |
| Private Enterprise | License | Private control plane, KMS, audit logs | Regulated/enterprise |

Discount and pilot notes:
- Early pilot customers for Dedicated get onboarding credits and a 3-month price lock. Sales should coordinate with finance for exceptions.

6) Release notes (v7 GA & Optimize v6 - 2026-11 release)
Release date: 2026-11-22
Highlights:
- GA: Policy-based routing and automatic fallback for hosted and dedicated customers.
- Console: cost-suggestion MVP added to per-route settings with estimated cost delta.
- Optimize: integrated quantization recommendation engine (v0.6) and one-click preview.
- Reliability: Storage and cache sharding improvements reduced cache eviction rates by 28% in internal benchmarks.

Notable bug fixes:
- Fixed tokenization mismatch for LLAMA-4 models that caused off-by-one truncation in a small fraction of edge prompts.
- Resolved a race condition in canary rollback logic under high-concurrency traffic.

Known issues and workarounds:
- Issue: Some private deployment edge cases require updated iptables rules during on-prem packaging. Workaround: follow onprem-packaging/iptables-compat guide; engineers should run the packaging script with --legacy-net flag.
- Issue: Cost estimator may underreport cost for complex multi-model routes. Workaround: enable debug estimator and cross-validate with billing logs.

7) Launch checklist and rollout plan
- Pre-launch (2 weeks out):
  1. Finalize SDK releases and API changelog (owner: Eng DevEx).
  2. Run scale test simulating 2x expected peak (owner: Eng SRE).
  3. Publish pricing and sales collateral (owner: GTM).
  4. Prepare support playbook and escalations (owner: Customer Success).

- Launch day:
  1. Flip feature flags for Router & Console (owner: Release Eng).
  2. Monitor SLO dashboards and error budgets (owner: Eng SRE).
  3. Notify customers via status page and targeted emails (owner: Customer Success).

- Post-launch (30 days):
  1. Weekly eval of rollout metrics (latency, cost delta, cache hit rate).
  2. Collect 3 pilot customer feedback sessions for Dedicated pricing.
  3. Triage and patch high-severity issues within SLA window.

8) Metrics and success criteria
- Adoption: % of active customers using routing policies within 60 days (target: 40%).
- Cost impact: median per-token cost delta for routes using Optimize suggestions (target: 15% reduction).
- Reliability: SLO compliance (99.9%/month for hosted).
- Quality: regressions in eval suites (should be <= 0.5% of prompt set).
